observation.visible_scene: A mostly still, top-down-ish view of a calm water surface acting as a mirror. Reflected dark tree trunks and bare branches run across the top; a broad patch of golden-tan foliage is reflected on the left-center; a bright sky/cloud reflection with a glare hotspot fills the far-left edge; a small spray of yellow leaves is reflected at the top-right; a few real leafy twigs poke up along the bottom edge. A circular watermark logo is fixed in the bottom-right corner in every frame.
visible_changes: The water keeps a gentle continuous ripple; the reflected sky/cloud region in the lower-center is broken into wavy bands that reshape and shift slightly from frame to frame.
The contours of the golden foliage reflection and the dark trunk reflection waver and distort at their edges as ripples pass, but their overall positions in the frame do not move.
The bright glare patch on the left edge fluctuates in shape and intensity while staying in place.
The bottom twigs and the top-right yellow-leaf reflection remain essentially fixed, indicating no camera pan.
All visible motion is deformation/shimmer of the reflections on the surface, not translation of separate objects across the scene.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the surface ripples (wind, a disturbance, etc.) is not shown.
The actual trees and sky being reflected are out of frame; only their mirror images are visible.
Whether the rippling continues, settles, or intensifies after the last frame is unknown.
uncertain_details: Any very slight camera drift cannot be confirmed; the consistent placement of the trunks, glare, bottom twigs and watermark supports a static camera.
The exact boundary between reflection and any real foreground leaves at the bottom is hard to separate.
